lines.text: Forty thousand years ago, a grandmother sings the road to the water: first verse, the big rock; second verse, the bent tree.
The children sing it back. It sounds like a song. It is a map.
Plain words are slippery: say a list once, and by nightfall the order is wrong.
But a beat holds words in line. A wrong word breaks the rhythm you can hear the mistake.
So what had to survive went into songs: where the water is, which plants heal, which plants kill.
Mouth to mouth, camp to camp, generation to generation a song a whole group depends on arrives almost unchanged.
Rhythm is a memory tool. A song remembers what plain words forget.
The first archive was a body. Then a story, then a mark. And riding through them all, a song.
You still use this tool. You learned your letters by singing them.
One idea at a time, across the whole story of this planet subscribe to Earth One.
